narrative: Markets have entered an acute risk-off regime as both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 plunge into correction territory, triggered by an unwinding of the AI trade following Anthropic's IPO. Liquidity has reached a 10-year low while the VIX has spiked above 30-35, amplifying selling pressure across equities and broader asset classes. Technology leaders are facing heavy scrutiny, exacerbated by an SEC accounting probe into Nvidia and reports challenging high-growth multiples. Indiscriminate cash-raising has broadened the selloff beyond tech into traditional safe havens like gold. Meanwhile, 10-year real rates holding near 3% and persistent geopolitical risks continue to weigh on equity valuations.

Nasdaq.why: Anchors report the index is down nearly 18% to 20% from its October peak, driven by fading AI enthusiasm, low liquidity, and regulatory scrutiny surrounding key chipmakers.

S&P 500.why: Christopher Cain and anchors note the benchmark is in correction territory after sliding over 10% from all-time highs amid broad-based equity liquidation.

Gold.why: Anchors note gold fell up to 4% (trading at $3,530 per ounce) as investors aggressively raise cash in an indiscriminate market de-risking.

Oil.why: Romaine Bostick points to a multi-week drop on ample supply and Brent hitting $91, while separate anchors noted modest crude gains and Alex Kokcharov highlighted shifting Russian export flows to Asia.

priced_in: Major indices entering correction territory and heightened volatility with the VIX holding above 30-35
Reduced probability of a December Fed interest rate hike
Transition to defensive positioning and an adjustment to prolonged higher-for-longer interest rates
debates: Crude trajectory: Romaine Bostick and anchors cite downward pressure to $91 Brent on ample supply and demand concerns, whereas other anchors note modest gains despite the market selloff.
Dollar direction: Anchors in one broadcast report a weaker dollar amid shifting flows, while another broadcast reports the US dollar strengthening by 4.56%.

AI fundamentals vs. price action: Debate over whether robust earnings estimates will stabilize tech or if sub-4% corporate AI adoption and high infrastructure costs necessitate further valuation resets.
